verses.en: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.
verses.pt: Fitando Paulo os olhos no sinédrio, disse: Varões irmãos, até o dia de hoje tenho andado diante de Deus com toda a boa consciência.
verses.en_web: Paul, looking steadfastly at the council, said, “Brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience until today.”
verses.en_bbe: And Paul, looking fixedly at the Sanhedrin, said, My brothers, my life has been upright before God till this day.

verses.en: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
verses.pt: Mas o sumo sacerdote, Ananias, mandou aos que estavam junto dele que o ferissem na boca.
verses.en_web: The high priest, Ananias, commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.
verses.en_bbe: And the high priest, Ananias, gave orders to those who were near him to give him a blow on the mouth.

verses.en: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?
verses.pt: Então Paulo lhe disse: Deus te ferirá a ti, parede branqueada; tu estás aí sentado para julgar-me segundo a lei, e contra a lei mandas que eu seja ferido?
verses.en_web: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to judge me according to the law, and command me to be struck contrary to the law?”
verses.en_bbe: Then Paul said to him, God will give blows to you, you whitewashed wall: are you here to be my judge by law, and by your orders am I given blows against the law?

verses.en: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?
verses.pt: Os que estavam ali disseram: Injurias o sumo sacerdote de Deus?
verses.en_web: Those who stood by said, “Do you malign God’s high priest?”
verses.en_bbe: And those who were near said, Do you say such words against God's high priest?

verses.en: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
verses.pt: Disse Paulo: Não sabia, irmãos, que era o sumo sacerdote; porque está escrito: Não dirás mal do príncipe do teu povo.
verses.en_web: Paul said, “I didn’t know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written, ‘You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.’”
verses.en_bbe: And Paul said, Brother, I had no idea that he was the high priest: for it has been said, You may not say evil about the ruler of your people.

verses.en: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
verses.pt: Sabendo Paulo que uma parte era de saduceus e outra de fariseus, clamou no sinédrio: Varões irmãos, eu sou fariseu, filho de fariseus; é por causa da esperança da ressurreição dos mortos que estou sendo julgado.
verses.en_web: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, “Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!”
verses.en_bbe: But when Paul saw that half of them were Sadducees and the rest Pharisees, he said in the Sanhedrin, Brothers, I am a Pharisee, and the son of Pharisees: I am here to be judged on the question of the hope of the coming back from the dead.

verses.en: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.
verses.pt: Ora, dizendo ele isto, surgiu dissensão entre os fariseus e saduceus; e a multidão se dividiu.
verses.en_web: When he had said this, an argument arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the crowd was divided.
verses.en_bbe: And when he had said this, there was an argument between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and a division in the meeting.

verses.en: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.
verses.pt: Porque os saduceus dizem que não há ressurreição, nem anjo, nem espírito; mas os fariseus reconhecem uma e outra coisa.
verses.en_web: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess all of these.
verses.en_bbe: For the Sadducees say that there is no coming back from the dead, and no angels or spirits: but the Pharisees have belief in all these.

verses.en: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees’ part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.
verses.pt: Daí procedeu grande clamor; e levantando-se alguns da parte dos fariseus, altercavam, dizendo: Não achamos nenhum mal neste homem; e, quem sabe se lhe falou algum espírito ou anjo?
verses.en_web: A great clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the Pharisees’ part stood up, and contended, saying, “We find no evil in this man. But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him, let’s not fight against God!”
verses.en_bbe: And there was a great outcry: and some of the scribes on the side of the Pharisees got up and took part in the discussion, saying, We see no evil in this man: what if he has had a revelation from an angel or a spirit?

verses.en: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.
verses.pt: E avolumando-se a dissenção, o comandante, temendo que Paulo fosse por eles despedaçado, mandou que os soldados descessem e o tirassem do meio deles e o levassem para a fortaleza.
verses.en_web: When a great argument arose, the commanding officer, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them, and bring him into the barracks.
verses.en_bbe: And when the argument became very violent, the chief captain, fearing that Paul would be pulled in two by them, gave orders to the armed men to take him by force from among them, and take him into the army building.

verses.en: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.
verses.pt: Na noite seguinte, apresentou-se-lhe o Senhor e disse: Tem bom ânimo: porque, como deste testemunho de mim em Jerusalém, assim importa que o dês também em Roma.
verses.en_web: The following night, the Lord stood by him, and said, “Cheer up, Paul, for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem, so you must testify also at Rome.”
verses.en_bbe: And the night after, the Lord came to his side and said, Be of good heart, for as you have been witnessing for me in Jerusalem, so will you be my witness in Rome.

verses.en: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
verses.pt: Quando já era dia, coligaram-se os judeus e juraram sob pena de maldição que não comeriam nem beberiam enquanto não matassem a Paulo.
verses.en_web: When it was day, some of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.
verses.en_bbe: And when it was day, the Jews came together and put themselves under an oath that they would take no food or drink till they had put Paul to death.

verses.en: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.
verses.pt: Eram mais de quarenta os que fizeram esta conjuração;
verses.en_web: There were more than forty people who had made this conspiracy.
verses.en_bbe: And more than forty of them took this oath.

verses.en: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.
verses.pt: e estes foram ter com os principais sacerdotes e anciãos, e disseram: Conjuramo-nos sob pena de maldição a não provarmos coisa alguma até que matemos a Paulo.
verses.en_web: They came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, “We have bound ourselves under a great curse, to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.
verses.en_bbe: And they came to the chief priests and the rulers and said, We have taken a great oath to take no food till we have put Paul to death

verses.en: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.
verses.pt: Agora, pois, vós, com o sinédrio, rogai ao comandante que o mande descer perante vós como se houvésseis de examinar com mais precisão a sua causa; e nós estamos prontos para matá-lo antes que ele chegue.
verses.en_web: Now therefore, you with the council inform the commanding officer that he should bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you were going to judge his case more exactly. We are ready to kill him before he comes near.”
verses.en_bbe: So now, will you and the Sanhedrin make a request to the military authorities to have him sent down to you, as if you were desiring to go into the business in greater detail; and we, before ever he gets to you, will be waiting to put him to death.

verses.en: And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.
verses.pt: Mas o filho da irmã de Paulo tendo sabido da cilada, foi, entrou na fortaleza e avisou a Paulo.
verses.en_web: But Paul’s sister’s son heard they were lying in wait, and he came and entered into the barracks and told Paul.
verses.en_bbe: But Paul's sister's son had word of their design, and he came into the army building and gave news of it to Paul.

verses.en: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.
verses.pt: Chamando Paulo um dos centuriões, disse: Leva este moço ao comandante, porque tem alguma coisa que lhe comunicar.
verses.en_web: Paul summoned one of the centurions, and said, “Bring this young man to the commanding officer, for he has something to tell him.”
verses.en_bbe: And Paul sent for a captain and said, Take this young man to your chief, for he has news for him.

verses.en: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.
verses.pt: Tomando-o ele, pois, levou-o ao comandante e disse: O preso Paulo, chamando-me, pediu-me que trouxesse à tua presença este moço, que tem alguma coisa a dizer-te.
verses.en_web: So he took him, and brought him to the commanding officer, and said, “Paul, the prisoner, summoned me and asked me to bring this young man to you, who has something to tell you.”
verses.en_bbe: So he took him to the chief captain and said, Paul, the prisoner, made a request to me to take this young man to you, for he has something to say to you.

verses.en: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that thou hast to tell me?
verses.pt: O comandante tomou-o pela mão e, retirando-se à parte, perguntou-lhe em particular: Que é que tens a contar-me?
verses.en_web: The commanding officer took him by the hand, and going aside, asked him privately, “What is it that you have to tell me?”
verses.en_bbe: And the chief took him by the hand and, going on one side, said to him privately, What is it you have to say to me?

verses.en: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.
verses.pt: Disse ele: Os judeus combinaram rogar-te que amanhã mandes Paulo descer ao sinédrio, como que tendo de inquirir com mais precisão algo a seu respeito;
verses.en_web: He said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though intending to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.
verses.en_bbe: And he said, The Jews are in agreement together to make a request to you for Paul to be taken, on the day after this, into the Sanhedrin, to be questioned in greater detail.

verses.en: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.
verses.pt: tu, pois, não te deixes persuadir por eles; porque mais de quarenta homens dentre eles armaram ciladas, os quais juraram sob pena de maldição não comerem nem beberem até que o tenham morto; e agora estão aprestados, esperando a tua promessa.
verses.en_web: Therefore don’t yield to them, for more than forty men lie in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse neither to eat nor to drink until they have killed him. Now they are ready, looking for the promise from you.”
verses.en_bbe: But do not give way to them, for more than forty of them are waiting for him, having taken an oath not to take food or drink till they have put him to death: and now they are ready, waiting for your order.

verses.en: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.
verses.pt: Então o comandante despediu o moço, ordenando-lhe que a ninguém dissesse que lhe havia contado aquilo.
verses.en_web: So the commanding officer let the young man go, charging him, “Tell no one that you have revealed these things to me.”
verses.en_bbe: So the chief captain let the young man go, saying to him, Do not say to anyone that you have given me word of these things.

verses.en: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;
verses.pt: Chamando dois centuriões, disse: Aprontai para a terceira hora da noite duzentos soldados de infantaria, setenta de cavalaria e duzentos lanceiros para irem até Cesaréia;
verses.en_web: He called to himself two of the centurions, and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, with seventy horsemen, and two hundred men armed with spears, at the third hour of the night.”
verses.en_bbe: And he sent for two captains and said, Make ready two hundred men, with seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, to go to Caesarea, at the third hour of the night:

verses.en: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.
verses.pt: e mandou que aparelhassem cavalgaduras para que Paulo montasse, a fim de o levarem salvo ao governador Félix.
verses.en_web: He asked them to provide animals, that they might set Paul on one, and bring him safely to Felix the governor.
verses.en_bbe: And get beasts so that they may put Paul on them, and take him safely to Felix, the ruler.

verses.en: And he wrote a letter after this manner:
verses.pt: E escreveu-lhe uma carta nestes termos:
verses.en_web: He wrote a letter like this:
verses.en_bbe: And he sent a letter in these words:

verses.en: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.
verses.pt: Cláudio Lísias, ao excelentíssimo governador Félix, saúde.
verses.en_web: “Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.
verses.en_bbe: Claudius Lysias, to the most noble ruler, Felix, peace be with you.

verses.en: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.
verses.pt: Este homem foi preso pelos judeus, e estava a ponto de ser morto por eles quando eu sobrevim com a tropa e o livrei ao saber que era romano.
verses.en_web: “This man was seized by the Jews, and was about to be killed by them, when I came with the soldiers and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.
verses.en_bbe: This man was taken by the Jews, and was about to be put to death by them, when I came on them with the army and took him out of danger, having knowledge that he was a Roman.

verses.en: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:
verses.pt: Querendo saber a causa por que o acusavam, levei-o ao sinédrio deles;
verses.en_web: Desiring to know the cause why they accused him, I brought him down to their council.
verses.en_bbe: And, desiring to get at the reason for their attack on him, I took him down to their Sanhedrin:

verses.en: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.
verses.pt: e achei que era acusado de questões da lei deles, mas que nenhum crime havia nele digno de morte ou prisão.
verses.en_web: I found him to be accused about questions of their law, but not to be charged with anything worthy of death or of imprisonment.
verses.en_bbe: Then it became clear to me that it was a question of their law, and that nothing was said against him which might be a reason for prison or death.

verses.en: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him. Farewell.
verses.pt: E quando fui informado que haveria uma cilada contra o homem, logo to enviei, intimando também aos acusadores que perante ti se manifestem contra ele. [Passa bem.]
verses.en_web: When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him to you immediately, charging his accusers also to bring their accusations against him before you. Farewell.”
verses.en_bbe: And when news was given to me that a secret design was being made against the man, I sent him straight away to you, giving orders to those who are against him to make their statements before you.

verses.en: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.
verses.pt: Os soldados, pois, conforme lhes fora mandado, tomando a Paulo, o levaram de noite a Antipátride.
verses.en_web: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
verses.en_bbe: So the armed men, as they were ordered, took Paul and came by night to Antipatris.

verses.en: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:
verses.pt: Mas no dia seguinte, deixando aos de cavalaria irem com ele, voltaram à fortaleza;
verses.en_web: But on the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks.
verses.en_bbe: But on the day after, they sent the horsemen on with him, and went back to their place:

verses.en: Who, when they came to Caesarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
verses.pt: os quais, logo que chegaram a Cesaréia e entregaram a carta ao governador, apresentaram-lhe também Paulo.
verses.en_web: When they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.
verses.en_bbe: And they, when they came to Caesarea, gave the letter to the ruler, and took Paul before him.

verses.en: And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;
verses.pt: Tendo lido a carta, o governador perguntou de que província ele era; e, sabendo que era da Cilícia,
verses.en_web: When the governor had read it, he asked what province he was from. When he understood that he was from Cilicia, he said,
verses.en_bbe: And after reading it, he said, What part of the country do you come from? And, hearing that he was from Cilicia,

verses.en: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s judgment hall.
verses.pt: disse: Ouvir-te-ei quando chegarem também os teus acusadores; e mandou que fosse guardado no pretório de Herodes.
verses.en_web: “I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive.” He commanded that he be kept in Herod’s palace.
verses.en_bbe: I will give hearing to your cause, he said, when those who are against you have come. And he gave orders for him to be kept in Herod's Praetorium.
